A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same calibrated deep clustering (CDC) work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original CDC experiments on six image benchmarks, including clustering, calibration, failure rejection, and component ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original sensitivity studies, repeated-run results, transfer evaluations, and out-of-distribution detection experiments.

M1.justification: The reported pseudo-label selection rule changes: v2 multiplies average confidence over all samples assigned to a class by floor(B/C), whereas v3 sums confidence over its top floor(B/C) samples and rounds down. This refines sample selection while retaining the dual-head architecture, losses, initialization, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: The original six benchmarks remain. Appendix C adds ImageNet50/100/200 subset evaluations and a distinct OOD-detection task using CIFAR and Tiny-ImageNet near-OOD inputs and SVHN, Textures, and Places365 far-OOD inputs, substantially broadening evaluated conditions.

E2.justification: Appendix C.1 adds evaluations of FlexMatch and FreeMatch thresholding both directly and integrated into CDC, plus CDC augmented with Gradient Synchronization Filter and Prototype Proximity Filter. These introduce substantive alternatives to CDC's sample-selection strategy. Comparator membership in the original benchmark tables is retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include transferring ImageNet-10 hyperparameters to larger ImageNet subsets with ResNet-50, evaluating OOD detection through maximum-softmax scores, and applying CDC for 100 epochs after SCAN or SeCu. The original six-benchmark splits, main training budgets, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds batch-size/mini-cluster sensitivity, hidden-width and expanded entropy-weight ablations, a label-smoothing sweep, alternative sample-selection analyses, hyperparameter transfer, and OOD robustness tests. Conversely, v2's all-versus-selected-samples head-training ablation and MLP-depth sweep disappear. The principal component ablations in Table 2 remain.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 newly specifies eight runs and reports mean and standard deviation for CDC and several baselines across all six benchmarks in Tables 10–11. v2 lacks explicit run counts and corresponding uncertainty tables. Table 5 additionally reports variability across hyperparameter settings, distinct from repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in the original Tables 1, 2, and 4 are unchanged, but substantial new results are added. For example, Table 12 reports ImageNet50 ACC/ECE of 77.8%/7.5% for CDC versus 76.8%/14.2% for SCAN-3 under the added setting. The CIFAR-20 calibration comparison in prose is corrected from 52.3%→40.6% to 52.3%→4.9%, matching both versions' Table 1.

T1.justification: v3 corrects Theorem 1's reversed region indices: confidence is penalized in unreliable region F and preserved in reliable region T, consistent with the existing proof. Appendix A.1 also adds an explicit feature-normalization assumption. The principal propositions, theorems, and derivations otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the headline calibration advantage from approximately 10× to 5× on average; the conclusion similarly reduces its stated factor. The central contributions concerning dual-head calibration, confidence-aware selection, initialization, and improved clustering remain.

C2.justification: New discussion explains mini-cluster penalty strength, SSL thresholding failures, initialization-related stability, computational tradeoffs, and applicability to other clustering models and OOD rejection. The explicit v2 limitation that cluster count must be known is removed, although v3 still assumes predefined clusters.

D1.justification: v3 adds a CDC code-access link, identifies the solo-learn library, describes K-means++ initialization and a PyTorch implementation, and reports parameter counts, runtime, and memory in Table 7. These supplement an otherwise largely retained implementation recipe; they do not establish that existing experiments changed.

R1.justification: Positioning expands beyond the original deep-clustering and supervised-calibration survey. v3 discusses CLIP-based SIC/TAC, distinguishes domain-adaptation calibration using labeled source data, and substantially relates CDC to moderately confident sample selection and FlexMatch/FreeMatch thresholding in Appendix C.1.

P1.justification: Contributions, related work, and several method explanations are extensively rewritten. Initialization moves from Section 3.1 to 3.3, Algorithm 1 moves from the appendix into the main method section, and experiments and appendices are reorganized. Citation style, affiliations, and conference headers also change.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR layout, revises framework labels, restructures tables, and adds sensitivity, sample-selection, and OOD displays. Existing appendix Figures 5–7 become Figures 6, 7, and 9 with retained content; Figures 5, 8, 10, and 11 provide new displays. Figure 3 also corrects ARPC to AURC.

improvement.justification: The eight-run uncertainty tables, relevant SSL comparisons, and transfer/OOD evaluations substantially strengthen evidence for CDC's stability and applicability beyond v2's original evaluations. Resource reporting and code-access information further improve reproducibility. Removed ablations and the explicit cluster-count limitation are drawbacks, as is overstated robustness prose: Table 5's CIFAR-20 ACC spans 58.1–62.6%, exceeding the claimed ±1.4-point variation. These issues temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial empirical strengthening.
